source: That whale of Stubb’s, so dearly purchased, was duly brought to the Pequod’s side, where all those cutting and hoisting operations previously detailed, were regularly gone through, even to the baling of the Heidelburgh Tun, or Case.

While some were occupied with this latter duty, others were employed in dragging away the larger tubs, so soon as filled with the sperm; and when the proper time arrived, this same sperm was carefully manipulated ere going to the try-works, of which anon.

It had cooled and crystallized to such a degree, that when, with several others, I sat down before a large Constantine’s bath of it, I found it strangely concreted into lumps, here and there rolling about in the liquid part. It was our business to squeeze these lumps back into fluid. A sweet and unctuous duty! No wonder that in old times this sperm was such a favourite cosmetic. Such a clearer! such a sweetener! such a softener! such a delicious molifier! After having my hands in it for only a few minutes, my fingers felt like eels, and began, as it were, to serpentine and spiralise.

As I sat there at my ease, cross-legged on the deck; after the bitter exertion at the windlass; under a blue tranquil sky; the ship under indolent sail, and gliding so serenely along; as I bathed my hands among those soft, gentle globules of infiltrated tissues, woven almost within the hour; as they richly broke to my fingers, and discharged all their opulence, like fully ripe grapes their wine; as I snuffed up that uncontaminated aroma,—literally and truly, like the smell of spring violets; I declare to you, that for the time I lived as in a musky meadow; I forgot all about our horrible oath; in that inexpressible sperm, I washed my hands and my heart of it; I almost began to credit the old Paracelsan superstition that sperm is of rare virtue in allaying the heat of anger; while bathing in that bath, I felt divinely free from all ill-will, or petulance, or malice, of any sort whatsoever.

Squeeze! squeeze! squeeze! all the morning long; I squeezed that sperm till I myself almost melted into it; I squeezed that sperm till a strange sort of insanity came over me; and I found myself unwittingly squeezing my co-laborers’ hands in it, mistaking their hands for the gentle globules. Such an abounding, affectionate, friendly, loving feeling did this avocation beget; that at last I was continually squeezing their hands, and looking up into their eyes sentimentally; as much as to say,—Oh! my dear fellow beings, why should we longer cherish any social acerbities, or know the slightest ill-humor or envy! Come; let us squeeze hands all round; nay, let us all squeeze ourselves into each other; let us squeeze ourselves universally into the very milk and sperm of kindness.

Would that I could keep squeezing that sperm for ever! For now, since by many prolonged, repeated experiences, I have perceived that in all cases man must eventually lower, or at least shift, his conceit of attainable felicity; not placing it anywhere in the intellect or the fancy; but in the wife, the heart, the bed, the table, the saddle, the fireside, the country; now that I have perceived all this, I am ready to squeeze case eternally. In thoughts of the visions of the night, I saw long rows of angels in paradise, each with his hands in a jar of spermaceti.
Now, while discoursing of sperm, it behooves to speak of other things akin to it, in the business of preparing the sperm whale for the try-works.

First comes white-horse, so called, which is obtained from the tapering part of the fish, and also from the thicker portions of his flukes. It is tough with congealed tendons—a wad of muscle—but still contains some oil. After being severed from the whale, the white-horse is first cut into portable oblongs ere going to the mincer. They look much like blocks of Berkshire marble.

Plum-pudding is the term bestowed upon certain fragmentary parts of the whale’s flesh, here and there adhering to the blanket of blubber, and often participating to a considerable degree in its unctuousness. It is a most refreshing, convivial, beautiful object to behold. As its name imports, it is of an exceedingly rich, mottled tint, with a bestreaked snowy and golden ground, dotted with spots of the deepest crimson and purple. It is plums of rubies, in pictures of citron. Spite of reason, it is hard to keep yourself from eating it. I confess, that once I stole behind the foremast to try it. It tasted something as I should conceive a royal cutlet from the thigh of Louis le Gros might have tasted, supposing him to have been killed the first day after the venison season, and that particular venison season contemporary with an unusually fine vintage of the vineyards of Champagne.

There is another substance, and a very singular one, which turns up in the course of this business, but which I feel it to be very puzzling adequately to describe. It is called slobgollion; an appellation original with the whalemen, and even so is the nature of the substance. It is an ineffably oozy, stringy affair, most frequently found in the tubs of sperm, after a prolonged squeezing, and subsequent decanting. I hold it to be the wondrously thin, ruptured membranes of the case, coalescing.

Gurry, so called, is a term properly belonging to right whalemen, but sometimes incidentally used by the sperm fishermen. It designates the dark, glutinous substance which is scraped off the back of the Greenland or right whale, and much of which covers the decks of those inferior souls who hunt that ignoble Leviathan.

Nippers. Strictly this word is not indigenous to the whale’s vocabulary. But as applied by whalemen, it becomes so. A whaleman’s nipper is a short firm strip of tendinous stuff cut from the tapering part of Leviathan’s tail: it averages an inch in thickness, and for the rest, is about the size of the iron part of a hoe. Edgewise moved along the oily deck, it operates like a leathern squilgee; and by nameless blandishments, as of magic, allures along with it all impurities.

But to learn all about these recondite matters, your best way is at once to descend into the blubber-room, and have a long talk with its inmates. This place has previously been mentioned as the receptacle for the blanket-pieces, when stript and hoisted from the whale. When the proper time arrives for cutting up its contents, this apartment is a scene of terror to all tyros, especially by night. On one side, lit by a dull lantern, a space has been left clear for the workmen. They generally go in pairs,—a pike-and-gaffman and a spade-man. The whaling-pike is similar to a frigate’s boarding-weapon of the same name. The gaff is something like a boat-hook. With his gaff, the gaffman hooks on to a sheet of blubber, and strives to hold it from slipping, as the ship pitches and lurches about. Meanwhile, the spade-man stands on the sheet itself, perpendicularly chopping it into the portable horse-pieces. This spade is sharp as hone can make it; the spademan’s feet are shoeless; the thing he stands on will sometimes irresistibly slide away from him, like a sledge. If he cuts off one of his own toes, or one of his assistants’, would you be very much astonished? Toes are scarce among veteran blubber-room men.

paragraphs: Stubb's whale, bought at such a high price, was brought alongside the Pequod in due course, and all the cutting and hoisting operations described earlier were carried out in the usual way, right down to bailing out the Heidelburgh Tun, or Case.

While some were occupied with this latter duty, others were employed in dragging away the larger tubs as soon as they were filled with sperm. And when the proper time arrived, this same sperm was carefully processed before going to the try-works, of which more later.

modern_da.title: Kapitel 94 — Et tryk af hånden
paragraphs: Stubbs hval, der var købt så dyrt, blev med tiden bragt ind langs siden af Pequod, og al den skæring og hejsning, der er beskrevet tidligere, blev udført på den sædvanlige måde, lige til udøsningen af Heidelburgh-tønden, eller Hovedkassen.

Mens nogle var optaget af den sidste opgave, var andre beskæftiget med at slæbe de større baljer væk, så snart de var fyldt med spermaceti. Og når den rette tid kom, blev denne samme spermaceti omhyggeligt bearbejdet, før den kom til tranværket, som der siges mere om senere.

Spermacetien var blevet så afkølet og krystalliseret, at da jeg satte mig sammen med flere andre foran en stor Konstantin-badekumme af den, fandt jeg ud af, at den ejendommeligt var stivnet til klumper, der trillede rundt her og der i væsken. Vores opgave var at klemme disse klumper ud til væske igen. En sød, fedtet pligt! Det er intet under, at denne spermaceti var en så populær skønhedscreme i gamle dage. Sikke en renser! Sikke en forsøder! Sikke en blødgører! Sikke en lækker beroliger! Efter at mine hænder havde været i den blot nogle få minutter, føltes mine fingre som ål og begyndte, så at sige, at slange og snirkle sig.

Jeg sad der i fred og ro med benene over kors på dækket — efter det bitre slid ved ankerspillet, under en blå, rolig himmel, mens skibet gled så fredeligt af sted under dovne sejl — og lod mine hænder bade mellem de bløde, milde klumper af gennemvædet væv, der næsten lige var blevet dannet, og som så rigt sprang op under mine fingre og gav al deres fylde fra sig, som fuldmodne druer deres vin. Jeg indåndede den uforurenede duft, der bogstaveligt og sandelig var som duften af vårviol — og jeg forsikrer dig, at jeg for en tid levede som på en duftende eng. Jeg glemte alt om vores frygtelige ed. I den uudsigelige sperm vaskede jeg både hænder og hjerte rene for den. Jeg var lige ved at tro på den gamle paracelsiske overtro, at sperm har en sjælden kraft til at dæmpe vredens hede. Mens jeg badede i det bad, følte jeg mig guddommeligt fri for al ondskab, al irritation og al slags nag overhovedet.

Klem! Klem! Klem! Hele formiddagen klemte jeg den sperm, til jeg næsten selv smeltede ind i den. Jeg klemte den sperm, til en underlig slags galskab kom over mig, og jeg opdagede, at jeg uden at tænke over det klemte mine medarbejderes hænder i den, fordi jeg forvekslede deres hænder med de bløde klumper. Det arbejde vakte sådan en overstrømmende, kærlig, venlig følelse i mig, at jeg til sidst hele tiden klemte deres hænder og så dem følsomt ind i øjnene — som for at sige: Å, mine kære medmennesker, hvorfor skulle vi længere nære nogen bitterhed mod hinanden eller kende til den mindste dårlige lune eller misundelse! Kom, lad os klemme hinandens hænder rundt omkring. Nej, lad os alle klemme os ind i hinanden. Lad os klemme os helt og holdent ind i selve mildhedens mælk og sperm.

Gid jeg kunne blive ved med at klemme den sperm for evigt! Lang og gentagen erfaring har lært mig, at et menneske i hvert enkelt tilfælde til sidst må sænke eller i det mindste flytte sin forestilling om den lykke, det kan nå — og placere den slet ikke i forstanden eller i fantasien, men i hustruen, hjertet, sengen, bordet, sadlen, ildstedet, landet. Nu, hvor jeg har set alt dette, er jeg parat til at klemme Hovedkassen i al evighed. I tankerne om nattens syner så jeg lange rækker af engle i paradis, hver med hænderne i en krukke spermaceti.
Nu, når vi taler om sperm, er det passende at nævne andre ting, der hører sammen med den i arbejdet med at gøre kaskelotten klar til tranværket.

Først er der det, man kalder hvidhest, som kommer fra den smalle del af fisken og fra de tykkere dele af hans halefinne. Det er sejt af størknede sener — en klump muskel — men det rummer alligevel noget olie. Når det er skåret af hvalen, bliver hvidhesten først hakket i aflange stykker, der er små nok til at bære, før den kommer til hakkeren. De ligner meget blokke af Berkshire-marmor.

Plumpudding er navnet på visse stumper af hvalens kød, som sidder hist og her fast på spækkappen og ofte har en god del af dens fedme. Det er noget af det mest forfriskende, festlige og smukke at se på. Som navnet antyder, har det en overordentlig rig, spættet farve: en stribet sneblød og gylden bund, drysset med pletter af det dybeste karmoisinrødt og purpur. Det er rubinrøde blommer sat i billeder af citronat. Mod al fornuft er det svært at holde sig fra at spise det. Jeg indrømmer, at jeg en gang listede om bag fokkemasten for at smage lidt. Det smagte nogenlunde, som jeg forestiller mig, at en kongelig kotelet fra låret af Ludvig den Tykke kunne have smagt — hvis han var blevet dræbt den første dag efter hjortejagtens sæson, og denne bestemte sæson var faldet sammen med en usædvanlig fin årgang i Champagnes vinmarker.

Der er endnu et stof, et meget enestående, som dukker op i løbet af dette arbejde, men som jeg har meget svært ved at beskrive ordentligt. Det kaldes slobgollion — et navn, som hvalfangerne selv har fundet på, og stoffet er lige så enestående. Det er noget ubeskriveligt grødet og trævlet, som oftest findes i spermkarrene efter en langvarig udpresning og efterfølgende aftapning. Jeg mener, at det er Hovedkassens forunderligt tynde, sprængte hinder, smeltet sammen.

Gurry, som det kaldes, er strengt taget et udtryk blandt rethvalfangere, selv om kaskelotfangerne nogle gange bruger det i forbifarten. Det betyder det mørke, klistrede stof, der bliver skrabet af ryggen på den grønlandske hval eller rethval, og en stor mængde af det ender med at dække dækkene hos de ringere sjæle, der jager den uædle Leviatan.

Nippers. Strengt taget hører ordet ikke hjemme i hvalens eget sprog. Men som hvalfangerne bruger det, bliver det det. En hvalfangers nipper er en kort, fast strimmel af senet stof, skåret af den smalle del af Leviatans hale. Den er i gennemsnit en tomme tyk og ellers omtrent på størrelse med jerndelen af en hakke. Når den føres på kant hen over det fedtede dæk, virker den som en skraber af læder, og ved navnløse lokkerier lokker den som ved trolddom alle urenheder med sig.

Men for at lære alt om disse obskure sager er det bedste at gå direkte ned i spækrummet og have en lang samtale med dem, der holder til der. Dette sted er tidligere blevet nævnt som beholderen for spækstykkerne, når de er flænset af og hejst op fra hvalen. Når tiden er inde til at skære indholdet op, bliver dette rum et skræmmende sted for alle nytilkomne, især om natten. På den ene side, oplyst af en mat lanterne, er der ryddet plads til arbejderne. De går som regel to og to — en pikmand og en spademand. Hvalpiken ligner en fregats entrevåben af samme navn. Gaffelen minder noget om en bådshage. Med sin gaffel hager gaffelmanden sig fast i en bane spæk og prøver at holde den fra at glide, mens skibet stamper og slingrer. Imens står spademanden oven på selve banen og hugger den lodret over i bærbare hestestykker. Denne spade er så skarp, som en slibesten kan gøre den. Spademandens fødder er skoløse. Det, han står på, glider nogle gange uimodståeligt væk under ham som en kane. Hvis han hugger en af sine egne tæer af, eller en af hjælpernes, ville du så blive meget overrasket? Tæer er sjældne blandt rutinerede mænd i spækrummet.
